title: IMO confirms tanker JIF BARRACUDA damaged off Khor Fakkan on 18 October
excerpt: The tanker was damaged with one seafarer injured northeast of Khor Fakkan, the IMO's confirmed incidents list says.
x_post: The IMO's confirmed incidents list records the tanker JIF BARRACUDA as damaged with one seafarer injured northeast of Khor Fakkan, UAE, on 18 October. #MaritimeSecurity #Shipping #Seafarers #StraitOfHormuz

lesson (facts): A named ship can be attacked twice: the IMO list carries the same vessel under separate dates, so check her earlier reco
lesson (writing): Never attach a claim made about an unnamed vessel to a named ship: give such a claim in its own sentence with the date a
notes: In the Strait of Hormuz and the Gulf section name the tanker struck off Bukha as the Kuwaiti-flagged Aframax AL DASMA, hit at 01:45 UTC on 21 October about 11 nautical miles west of Bukha, Oman, with the fire extinguished and all crew safe; carry the name in the headline, standfirst, lede, paragraph, key points and tweet, and say the IMO list dates the strike 20 October while UKMTO warning 179-26 gives 21 October.

In the same section call JIF BARRACUDA a Dutch-flagged tug, not a tanker, in the standfirst, key points, paragraph and tweet, and do not present UKMTO warning 177-26's tug struck by two projectiles as a second vessel: it is the same incident, and the injury is one minor casualty.

Remove the sentence crediting JIF BARRACUDA with a sea mine claim by Iran's Revolutionary Guards: the Guards' 20 October mine claims named no vessel and gCaptain reported them as unsubstantiated, so keep the mine claim only in the paragraph about those claims.

In the Earlier in the week Gulf paragraph name the tanker struck southeast of Al Faw as the Greek-owned, Liberian-flagged products tanker SOYIA, hit 30 nautical miles southeast of Al Faw at 18:30 UTC on 20 October with no damage reported and all crew safe, per UKMTO warning 180-26 and Seatrade.

In the Black Sea section report the Able's sinking as an update to her 6 October attack: say the Palau-flagged general cargo ship, hit 70 nautical miles east of Byala while carrying barley to Turkey, drifted unmanned and sank off the Turkish coast after vanishing from radar late on 19 October.
